title: kithd: discovery probe client (tailnet accept-any-cert HTTP GET)
description:
A small HTTP client that probes a single IP:port for a kithd instance. Accepts self-signed TLS certs — this is safe because traffic travels over Tailscale (which provides identity guarantees at the network layer), so we do not need TLS cert identity for security.

What: A standalone async function probe_peer(ip: &str, port: u16) -> Option<PeerSession> in a new kithd/src/discovery.rs module. No message delivery — read-only GET.

Algorithm:
1. Create kithd/src/discovery.rs.

2. Define PeerSession struct:
   - owner_user_id: String
   - owner_login: String
   - owner_display_name: Option<String>
   - mailbox_host: String  (extracted from api_url hostname:port)

3. Implement a TailnetCertVerifier that accepts any certificate:
   use rustls::client::danger::ServerCertVerifier;
   struct TailnetCertVerifier;
   // verify_server_cert: always returns Ok(ServerCertVerified::assertion())
   // verify_tls12_signature / verify_tls13_signature: delegate to CryptoProvider
   // supported_verify_schemes: delegate to CryptoProvider
   This is safe: Tailscale guarantees IP-to-identity; TLS provides confidentiality only.
   Add a doc comment: '// Safety: Tailscale network layer provides identity guarantees for tailnet IPs; cert is only needed for encryption, not authentication.'

4. Build an HTTP client using hyper + hyper-rustls (already in workspace) configured with TailnetCertVerifier:
   let tls_config = rustls::ClientConfig::builder()
     .dangerous()
     .with_custom_certificate_verifier(Arc::new(TailnetCertVerifier))
     .with_no_client_auth();
   let connector = HttpsConnectorBuilder::new()
     .with_tls_config(tls_config)
     .https_only()
     .enable_http1()
     .build();
   let client = Client::builder(TokioExecutor::new()).build(connector);

5. pub async fn probe_peer(ip: &str, port: u16) -> Option<PeerSession>:
   - Construct URL: format!('https://{}:{}/.well-known/jmap', ip, port)
   - Set timeout: 5 seconds (tokio::time::timeout)
   - GET the URL with a 'Host' header set to ip (or just bare IP URL)
   - On any error (timeout, connection refused, TLS error, non-200): return None
   - On 200: parse body as JSON into a minimal SessionProbe struct containing ownerUserId, ownerLogin, ownerDisplayName (optional), apiUrl
   - Extract mailbox_host from apiUrl: parse URL, take host + optional :port (omit :443)
   - If apiUrl parse fails: use ip:port as fallback mailbox_host
   - Return Some(PeerSession { ... })

6. Tests:
   - Test 1: a mock that returns a valid JMAP session JSON; assert PeerSession has correct fields.
   - Test 2: connection refused (probe to a port with nothing listening); assert returns None within timeout.
   - Test 3: HTTP 404 response; assert returns None.
   - Test 4: non-kith JSON response (missing ownerUserId); assert returns None.
   (Use a tokio::test with a minimal in-process HTTP server for tests 1 and 3.)

Defensive programming rules:
- Hard 5-second timeout on every probe (non-negotiable)
- Never panic on malformed JSON response (use Option/Result)
- Never log the raw session body (may contain user identity info)
- TailnetCertVerifier only used for probing, never for peer delivery
- probe_peer is fire-and-forget safe: all errors return None
